what: Intuit makes financial software. TurboTax prepares US tax returns, QuickBooks runs the books for small businesses, Credit Karma shows consumers their credit and offers them loans, and Mailchimp handles marketing emails.
customers: About 93 million consumers, small and mid-market businesses, and the accountants who serve them.
money: QuickBooks subscriptions, payroll, payments and Mailchimp
TurboTax, concentrated in the US tax season
fees from lenders when consumers take offers
moat: Once a business keeps its books in QuickBooks, moving years of records and retraining its accountant is painful; TurboTax carries prior-year data forward the same way.
risks: Any government move toward free direct tax filing threatens TurboTax
Consumer tax revenue is concentrated in a few months each year
Credit Karma income depends on lenders' appetite to make loans
Competition in small business accounting is intensifying
opportunities: Moving upmarket into mid-sized businesses raises revenue per customer substantially
Payments and payroll attached to QuickBooks grow faster than the software itself
AI assistants that do bookkeeping work are being sold as a higher-priced tier
watch: Online ecosystem revenue growth and TurboTax units during the tax season.
